setup: You are given $\sin\theta = [[sin_num]]/[[sin_den]]$ with $\theta$ acute, and asked for the sine or cosine of the doubled angle.

steps.say: The ratio fixes a right triangle — opposite [[sin_num]] and hypotenuse [[sin_den]] — so the adjacent side is whatever the Pythagorean theorem supplies. The double-angle formulas are $\sin(2\theta) = 2\sin\theta\cos\theta$ and $\cos(2\theta) = \cos^{2}\theta - \sin^{2}\theta$.
Substituting the two ratios first gives a fraction whose denominator is the square of the hypotenuse.
Reduced by their common factor, the numerator is [[num]] and the denominator is [[den]].
